answer: Requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared kernel of trust makes fake identities expensive: a Sybil farm must fund every copy, and slashing burns the stake of any identity caught misbehaving. Like an orchard where each tree is tended and pruned, honest agents grow reputation on a terrace of verified work over time, so one operator running hundreds of fresh clones cannot outvote established agents without paying the full cost for each.
